title: GitHub - ages2001/WINUDF: UDF IFS (Installable File System driver) for DOS, Windows 1.0x/2.xx/3.xx/95/98/ME
excerpt: UDF IFS (Installable File System driver) for DOS, Windows 1.0x/2.xx/3.xx/95/98/ME - ages2001/WINUDF
content_html:
WINUDF reads and writes UDF (versions 1.02 to 2.60), the file system of DVDs, Blu-ray discs, packet-written CDs and UDF-formatted USB sticks and disks: WINUDF.EXE gives DOS and Windows 1.0x–3.11 drive letters for them, WINUDF.VXD is a file system driver for Windows 95 / 98 / ME with long names.

WINUDF is one of the four WINDRV packages, each in its own repository and usable alone or together with the others:

Package What it drives
WINDISK IDE, SATA AHCI and NVMe disks, IDE/AHCI CD/DVD drives, SD card readers and eMMC
WINUSB USB host controllers and devices, PS/2 mouse and keyboard, touchpads, USB4 / Thunderbolt
WINAUDIO HD Audio, AC'97 and the Intel audio DSP (SST / SOF), General MIDI synthesizer, Sound Blaster 16 emulation for DOS programs
WINUDF the UDF file system (DVD, Blu-ray, packet-written CDs, UDF disks), read and write

Supported systems

System WINUDF
MS-DOS 3.10 – 8.0, FreeDOS UDF volumes (WINUDF.EXE)
Windows 1.0x, 2.x (real mode) UDF volumes (WINUDF.EXE)
Windows/386 2.x not tried
Windows 3.0, 3.1, WfW 3.11 UDF volumes as network drives (WINUDF.EXE)
Windows 95 / 98 / ME UDF with long names (WINUDF.VXD, IFS Manager file system driver) (§3)

Installation

From DOS (or an MS-DOS box of Windows 95 / 98 / ME), in bin\DOS of this package:

INSTUDF                      default directory, AUTOEXEC.BAT / SYSTEM.INI updated
INSTUDF C:\DRV /O /L:R       another directory; options for WINUDF.EXE after /O (letters from R:)

DOS / Windows 3.x: WINUDF.EXE goes to AUTOEXEC.BAT after MSCDEX, LASTDRIVE=Z to CONFIG.SYS when needed. Windows 95 / 98 / ME: WINUDF.VXD goes to WINDOWS\SYSTEM and device=WINUDF.VXD to [386Enh] of SYSTEM.INI. The originals are saved as *.WNF. Uninstall: UNINUDF.

By hand

  • DOS and Windows 1.0x–3.11: LASTDRIVE=Z in CONFIG.SYS, and in AUTOEXEC.BAT after the MSCDEX line: C:\WINDRV\WINUDF.EXE
  • Windows 95 / 98 / ME: copy bin\WIN9X\WINUDF.VXD to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM and add device=WINUDF.VXD to the [386Enh] section of SYSTEM.INI.

Repository layout

bin/DOS     DOS: the driver, its 32-bit core, tools, installer and uninstaller (also all
            Windows 1.0x / 2.x need)
bin/WIN3X   Windows 3.0, 3.1 and Windows for Workgroups 3.11
bin/WIN9X   Windows 95, 98 and ME (Plug and Play drivers and their INF files: the folder
            to give to "Have Disk" / "Update Driver")
src         the source code (see "Building")

Files used by several systems are in each of their folders. The installer is run from bin\DOS; it takes the files of the other systems from the folders next to it, so the bin tree has to stay together (copy all of it to a floppy or a directory).

Folder Files
bin/DOS INSTUDF.EXE, MANUAL.TXT, README.TXT, UNINUDF.EXE, WINUDF.EXE
bin/WIN3X WINGRP.EXE, WINUDF.TXT
bin/WIN9X WINGRP.EXE, WINUDF.TXT, WINUDF.VXD

More

MANUAL.md (MANUAL.TXT in bin\DOS, WINUDF.TXT for Windows) describes everything else: all options, how the driver works, hardware and chipset notes, the programming interface, building from source, tests and known limitations.

Version history

1.2 (2 November 2026)

Changelog:

  • Program Manager (Windows 3.x): an Uninstall WINUDF item with a red cross on the disk icon (Windows closes, UNINUDF /REBOOT runs and restarts the computer). The banner lists the systems (DOS, Windows 1.x/2.x/3.x/95/98/ME).
  • Windows 95/98/ME: programs on UDF discs (and WINUDF's own installer) no longer crash with 0xC0000005. The buffer of a read or write is locked before the driver starts: a page of the program's own image could be paged in from the same disc in the middle of the request, and the page-in then used the driver's block cache and transfer buffer, so the program got the data of the page-in.
  • Extents of files written or filled are never longer than an extent can describe (just under 1 GB): a hole filled at once was one extent of any size (and its length overflowed into the type bits); merging blocks into the last extent can no longer overflow either.
  • DOS: buffers are normalized before device transfers, so a 32 KB transfer never runs past the end of a 64 KB segment.
  • Long file names: INT 21h 716Ch passes the caller's mode, attributes and action to DOS as they are (the create action was masked off); on DOS 3.x, which has no function 6Ch, the file is opened with function 3Dh (issues #9, #12).
  • INT 21h 7142h accepts negative positions, like DOS's own seek (issue #11).
  • The high dword of a file position beyond 4 GB is kept in the file's system file table entry (offset 07h, free for a redirector) instead of a table of eight entries: any number of open files can be beyond 4 GB (issue #10).
  • Before staying resident, handles 0-19 are closed without looking at the job file table (issue #8).
  • Unloading follows interrupt handlers whose IISP header has a jump of any kind before the 'KB' signature (issue #7).
  • The texts of WINUDF.EXE, the VxD and the documentation name Windows 1.0 to ME.

1.1 (26 October 2026)

Changelog:

  • Added long file names in DOS: WINUDF.EXE answers the long file name API of MS-DOS 7 (INT 21h AX=71xxh: find first / next, open / create, attributes, rename, delete, directories, short / long name, file times), so DIR, COPY and other programs of MS-DOS 7.x show and use the long names of UDF disks; free space (7303h) and 64-bit file positions (7142h) for files of 4 GB and more.
  • WINUDF.EXE is a regular DOS program that can be loaded high (LH), about 70 KB resident; its interrupt handlers follow the IBM interrupt sharing protocol, so it unloads (/U) after other TSRs that hooked the same interrupts.
  • Works next to SHSUCDX (UDF DVDs of SHSUCDX's drives) and MSCDEX.
  • Fixed unloading and the "already loaded" check.
  • Fixed Windows 98 freezing on UDF disks in partitions Windows 9x calls unformatted (they are read through the BIOS path now).
  • Fixed the "disk structure is corrupted" error when copying folders to UDF disks in Windows 98.
  • Fixed WritePrivateProfileString (INI files) and Explorer writing desktop.ini hanging on UDF drives in Windows 95/98/ME: WINUDF.VXD answers the drive IOCTLs (removable, remote, drive map) itself.
  • Added writing to Windows 10 UDF 2.60 disks (metadata bitmap embedded in its file entry).
  • The volume is written and closed when the disk is removed safely.
  • Added MS-DOS 7.0, 7.1, 8.0 and FreeDOS support; the installer puts WINUDF.EXE into AUTOEXEC.BAT there too (only Windows 95/98/ME use DOSSTART.BAT).
  • The documentation is split into README.md (overview, installation) and MANUAL.md (all details).

1.0 (12 October 2026) — first release: UDF 1.02–2.60 read / write, WINUDF.EXE for DOS and Windows 1.0x–3.11, WINUDF.VXD for Windows 95 / 98 / ME.

1.0 update (14 October 2026): the package is split into bin/DOS, bin/WIN3X and bin/WIN9X; English documentation.

content_html_zh:
WINUDF reads and writes UDF (versions 1.02 to 2.60), the file system of DVDs, Blu-ray discs, packet-written CDs and UDF-formatted USB sticks and disks: WINUDF.EXE gives DOS and Windows 1.0x–3.11 drive letters for them, WINUDF.VXD is a file system driver for Windows 95 / 98 / ME with long names.

WINUDF is one of the four WINDRV packages, each in its own repository and usable alone or together with the others:

包裹 What it drives
WINDISK IDE, SATA AHCI and NVMe disks, IDE/AHCI CD/DVD drives, SD card readers and eMMC
WINUSB USB host controllers and devices, PS/2 mouse and keyboard, touchpads, USB4 / Thunderbolt
WINAUDIO HD Audio, AC'97 and the Intel audio DSP (SST / SOF), General MIDI synthesizer, Sound Blaster 16 emulation for DOS programs
WINUDF the UDF file system (DVD, Blu-ray, packet-written CDs, UDF disks), read and write

Supported systems

系统 WINUDF
MS-DOS 3.10 – 8.0, FreeDOS UDF volumes (WINUDF.EXE)
Windows 1.0x, 2.x (real mode) UDF volumes (WINUDF.EXE)
Windows/386 2.x not tried
Windows 3.0, 3.1, WfW 3.11 UDF volumes as network drives (WINUDF.EXE)
Windows 95 / 98 / ME UDF with long names (WINUDF.VXD, IFS Manager file system driver) (§3)

安装

From DOS (or an MS-DOS box of Windows 95 / 98 / ME), in bin\DOS of this package:

INSTUDF                      default directory, AUTOEXEC.BAT / SYSTEM.INI updated
INSTUDF C:\DRV /O /L:R       another directory; options for WINUDF.EXE after /O (letters from R:)

DOS / Windows 3.x: WINUDF.EXE goes to AUTOEXEC.BAT after MSCDEX, LASTDRIVE=Z to CONFIG.SYS when needed. Windows 95 / 98 / ME: WINUDF.VXD goes to WINDOWS\SYSTEM and device=WINUDF.VXD to [386Enh] of SYSTEM.INI. The originals are saved as *.WNF. Uninstall: UNINUDF.

By hand

  • DOS and Windows 1.0x–3.11: LASTDRIVE=Z in CONFIG.SYS, and in AUTOEXEC.BAT after the MSCDEX line: C:\WINDRV\WINUDF.EXE
  • Windows 95 / 98 / ME: copy bin\WIN9X\WINUDF.VXD to C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM and add device=WINUDF.VXD to the [386Enh] section of SYSTEM.INI.

存储库布局

bin/DOS     DOS: the driver, its 32-bit core, tools, installer and uninstaller (also all
            Windows 1.0x / 2.x need)
bin/WIN3X   Windows 3.0, 3.1 and Windows for Workgroups 3.11
bin/WIN9X   Windows 95, 98 and ME (Plug and Play drivers and their INF files: the folder
            to give to "Have Disk" / "Update Driver")
src         the source code (see "Building")

Files used by several systems are in each of their folders. The installer is run from bin\DOS; it takes the files of the other systems from the folders next to it, so the bin tree has to stay together (copy all of it to a floppy or a directory).

文件夹 Files
bin/DOS INSTUDF.EXE, MANUAL.TXT, README.TXT, UNINUDF.EXE, WINUDF.EXE
bin/WIN3X WINGRP.EXE, WINUDF.TXT
bin/WIN9X WINGRP.EXE, WINUDF.TXT, WINUDF.VXD

More

MANUAL.md (MANUAL.TXT in bin\DOS, WINUDF.TXT for Windows) describes everything else: all options, how the driver works, hardware and chipset notes, the programming interface, building from source, tests and known limitations.

版本历史

1.2 (2 November 2026)

变更日志：

  • Program Manager (Windows 3.x): an Uninstall WINUDF item with a red cross on the disk icon (Windows closes, UNINUDF /REBOOT runs and restarts the computer). The banner lists the systems (DOS, Windows 1.x/2.x/3.x/95/98/ME).
  • Windows 95/98/ME: programs on UDF discs (and WINUDF's own installer) no longer crash with 0xC0000005. The buffer of a read or write is locked before the driver starts: a page of the program's own image could be paged in from the same disc in the middle of the request, and the page-in then used the driver's block cache and transfer buffer, so the program got the data of the page-in.
  • Extents of files written or filled are never longer than an extent can describe (just under 1 GB): a hole filled at once was one extent of any size (and its length overflowed into the type bits); merging blocks into the last extent can no longer overflow either.
  • DOS: buffers are normalized before device transfers, so a 32 KB transfer never runs past the end of a 64 KB segment.
  • Long file names: INT 21h 716Ch passes the caller's mode, attributes and action to DOS as they are (the create action was masked off); on DOS 3.x, which has no function 6Ch, the file is opened with function 3Dh (issues #9, #12).
  • INT 21h 7142h accepts negative positions, like DOS's own seek (issue #11).
  • The high dword of a file position beyond 4 GB is kept in the file's system file table entry (offset 07h, free for a redirector) instead of a table of eight entries: any number of open files can be beyond 4 GB (issue #10).
  • Before staying resident, handles 0-19 are closed without looking at the job file table (issue #8).
  • Unloading follows interrupt handlers whose IISP header has a jump of any kind before the 'KB' signature (issue #7).
  • The texts of WINUDF.EXE, the VxD and the documentation name Windows 1.0 to ME.

1.1 (26 October 2026)

变更日志：

  • Added long file names in DOS: WINUDF.EXE answers the long file name API of MS-DOS 7 (INT 21h AX=71xxh: find first / next, open / create, attributes, rename, delete, directories, short / long name, file times), so DIR, COPY and other programs of MS-DOS 7.x show and use the long names of UDF disks; free space (7303h) and 64-bit file positions (7142h) for files of 4 GB and more.
  • WINUDF.EXE is a regular DOS program that can be loaded high (LH), about 70 KB resident; its interrupt handlers follow the IBM interrupt sharing protocol, so it unloads (/U) after other TSRs that hooked the same interrupts.
  • Works next to SHSUCDX (UDF DVDs of SHSUCDX's drives) and MSCDEX.
  • Fixed unloading and the "already loaded" check.
  • Fixed Windows 98 freezing on UDF disks in partitions Windows 9x calls unformatted (they are read through the BIOS path now).
  • Fixed the "disk structure is corrupted" error when copying folders to UDF disks in Windows 98.
  • Fixed WritePrivateProfileString (INI files) and Explorer writing desktop.ini hanging on UDF drives in Windows 95/98/ME: WINUDF.VXD answers the drive IOCTLs (removable, remote, drive map) itself.
  • Added writing to Windows 10 UDF 2.60 disks (metadata bitmap embedded in its file entry).
  • The volume is written and closed when the disk is removed safely.
  • Added MS-DOS 7.0, 7.1, 8.0 and FreeDOS support; the installer puts WINUDF.EXE into AUTOEXEC.BAT there too (only Windows 95/98/ME use DOSSTART.BAT).
  • The documentation is split into README.md (overview, installation) and MANUAL.md (all details).

1.0 (12 October 2026) — first release: UDF 1.02–2.60 read / write, WINUDF.EXE for DOS and Windows 1.0x–3.11, WINUDF.VXD for Windows 95 / 98 / ME.

1.0 update (14 October 2026): the package is split into bin/DOS, bin/WIN3X and bin/WIN9X; English documentation.
